value.name: Sonoma Clean Power
value.notes: Sonoma Clean Power is the public power provider for Sonoma and Mendocino counties, serving all incorporated cities in Sonoma County except Healdsburg (its own municipal utility) and Ukiah (Mendocino County). PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service. This membership fact is based on Sonoma Clean Power's own public description rather than a directly fetched member-list page (sonomacleanpower.org's dedicated service-area page returned HTTP 404 this session).

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

value: Request an inspection via the Permits & Planning Hub, by email at building@cityofpetaluma.org, or by phone (707-778-4479); scheduling occurs within 24 hours during regular business hours
Inspections are performed Monday-Thursday only; the next-day cutoff is 2:00 p.m. (a Friday inspection can be requested by phone for a minimum $514 fee)
Check the daily inspection schedule for the estimated 2-hour arrival window based on inspection order number
Keep the inspection card posted at the job site until the project passes final inspection
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Inspections process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City's page does not describe a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.
